content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents an anti-forwarding method with privacy preserving capacities with direct application images in social media. The encoder-scanning architecture is claimed to be robust to several distortions and noise sources introduced directly in the training, such as croping, debluring, rotation, perspective warping, pixel noise and JPEG compression. Experiments show robustness of the method against user introduced distortions and against adversarial attacks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengthes:

1) the paper presents a very interesting and important application of watermarking. the paper is very well motivated.
2) the method presented outperforms existing methods of the state of the art and show resilience against attacks
3) the method shows that it can be easily applied to unseen data, with small drop in the performance

Weaknesses:

1) the paper misses several explanations and details, so reproducibility is very difficult for this paper. Specifically, the authors explain that a UNet architecture is used for the encoder, but there is seldom details about the whole architecture, and also about the training network.

2) The paper does not present results or even mention one very common image manipulation which is scaling/resizing, which can destroy the watermarking information. This is a so common image manipulation that it seems odd that the authors did not consider it for the attacks. It should not be confused with image compression which is studied but it is a totally different manipulation.

3) The paper does not cite, mention or compare with another paper in the literature that creates a protection of images for security reasons, namely protecting portraits of ID documents. The paper is:

F. Shadmand, I. Medvedev and N. Gonc̗alves, "CodeFace: A Deep Learning Printer-Proof Steganography for Face Portraits," in IEEE Access, vol. 9, pp. 167282-167291, 2021, doi: 10.1109/ACCESS.2021.3132581.

4) It is not clear whether the watermarked information introduced to the images is always equal (somehow like a stamp) or it changes depending on the image itself. When compared to StegaStamp [Tancik 2020], for instance, there is a URL encoded in the image which significantly difficult the problem. It should be clear in the text that these differences also influences a fair comparison against the state of the art.

5) When comparing to the state of the art, there is a fundamental difference between for instance StegaStamp [Tancik, 2020], or even the paper not mentioned [Shadmand, 2021], that is the fact that these two methods protect images against printing, which introduces a significantly tougher scenario. The authors should make clear these differences for the sake of fair comparison.

6) It is not very clear if a brute force attack, pairing original and encoded images, would be able to reproduce the encoder. This is a serious threaten to the system, so the authors should discuss it.

7) Sec. 4.3 - it is not clear to me that this method presents a method that smartly hides the watermark according to "semantic representation". The watermark is dependent of the image itself, but I did not see evidence that it is a semantic variation of it. Whether I understand what the authors want to say, I do not agree with the way it is written.

Minor issues:

8) page 3 - "instead" , not "instread"
9) page 5, after equation (2), the expression of L_ps is missing a parenthesis
10) sec. 3.3 - DRAFT is DeepRAFT, correct?
11) page 6 - "smooth", not "smoothe"
12) page 9 - "zero-shot", not "zero-short", correct? - appears twice
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is mostly clear enough, except for the architecture and implementation details. It presents a novel and interesting method but lacks in terms of reproducibility. Please read my previous comments.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is interesting but has some weaknesses. I think that the paper would benefit of being rewritten focusing in the mentioned less positive points.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose a watermarking method that discourages users from forwarding media (particularly images) when they are not supposed to. The method works by adding imperceptible noise when the "anti-forwarding" mode is selected and scans images of recipients to make detect any unauthorized forwards. The method follows a GAN-like setup, using a generative model to craft perturbations, along with a scanner that uses tricks like data augmentation and robustness to maximize detection accuracy, and thus the quality of added perturbations.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strengths

- Section 4.5: "This suggests that DeepRAFT can be...." The inclusion of practical augmentation tricks, with the inclusion of adversarial inputs, is a great proof-of-concept and demonstrates that the proposed technique is applicable to actual systems if it can be deployed properly.

- The paper is well written and easy to follow, with the threat model (and the problem posed by it) easy to understand, and the proposed loss functions and techniques explained very well.

## Weaknesses

I reviewed the same paper for NeurIPS. While many of the weaknesses have been addressed, a few critical ones still remain:

- My biggest issue is the threat model proposed in this work. Most sensitive document sharing happens over physical documents, e-mails, or password-protected files at the very least. As far as sensitive images go, most messaging apps provide "private-chat" features that provide auto-delete functionalities with timers. The motivating examples are not convincing.
- Section 3.3 "..following most deployed.... keeps the watermark encoder as secret": obfuscation might be key here. The adversaries are unaware of the victim's exact defense. What about an adaptive adversary- one that has white-box access and can perturb examples more efficiently?
- Deploying the defense would mean all users would have to grant the messaging app permission to process all their images, which is very unlikely to happen (especially when using end-to-end encrypted chats with self-destruct images).
- The motivating examples mentioned 'documents', but none of the experiments/datasets seem to be related to images of documents. It is thus hard to know whether the proposed approach works well on such data as well, which is perhaps the stronger motivating factor (compared to normal images)
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
__Clarity__: The paper is well written: the motivation behind design choices, threat model, and results, are all described very clearly.

__Quality and Novelty__: I do not see much difference between the current defense setup and a standard GAN setup- the Encoder model is the generator, and the scanner model is the discriminator.

__Reproducibility__: The described system is fairly complicated. While most hyper-parameters are provided (and should be sufficient to get similar results), the community would benefit from a shared implementation as well.

### Minor Comments

- Page 1: "Billions of people..." please add a reference.
- Please also change the font style for 'green pipeline' and 'red pipeline': the paper should be color-blind friendly.
- PGD is known to be a strictly better attack than FGSM, so adding both in evaluations doesn't make a lot of sense. The authors might want to consider using another kind of attack instead of FGSM or completely removing it. Similarly, auto-attack already includes Auto-PGD, and I am unsure if there is any value in including both simultaneously (and even PGD, for that matter).
- Table 3 is very crowded- please consider re-formatting, splitting, etc.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed technique very clearly works across multiple types of data transforms (many of which are meant to simulate real-world situations when taking screenshots, etc.) and even adversarial inputs, but I am not fully convinced of the threat model and the proposed solution's feasibility itself. If the authors can make the problem statement (and the solution pipeline) more convincing,I might change my mind.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper first defines the anti-forwarding problem, in which a watermarked image is supposed to be detected for the purpose to stop unauthorized forwarding to unintended parties (presumably through public communication channels). 

The paper proposes a DNN based scheme, in which an encoder and and a scanner are jointly trained. The encoder is responsible for embed invisible watermarks into images to be protected, while the scanner is able to reliably detect the embedded watermarks to report potential abuse of the image in question. 

Robustness of watermark detection are demonstrated under a variety of settings including common image corruption as well as adversarial attacks. Zero-shot transferablity is also illustrated.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is well-written and easy to follow; 

The main problem statements is not well-defined, making the contribution of the work questionable;

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors develop a novel DeepRAFT system to protect users’ privacy via injecting non-fragile and visible watermarks. The devised system specifically comprises an encoder that incorporates the invisible stamp, and a canner that learns to detect such watermarks. Experiments on MirFlickr and Metfaces validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Pros:**
- The study on adversarial robustness is provided.
- The proposed setting of anti-forwarding seems novel.
- It is good to see the discussions of the method at the case of a series of differentiable image corruptions.

**Cons:**

- *Problem setting* 

The explored problem of anti-forwarding seems novel, which protects the privacy in image transmission among users. But on the application side, if one user would like to share a private image with a friend and meanwhile prevent the image from sharing among other uses, it seems trivial to set up a complicated system to identify the private image with such additional computational cost and time, since the DeepRAFT scanner needs to go through every image that is uploaded by the user. A currently more commonly adopted method in industrial applications for protecting the user privacy is to incorporate a watermarking stamp that shows the *name* of the person who shares this corresponding picture, which can prevent the privacy leakage in more cases. 

The authors may argue that this manner would degrade the quality of the shared image with the watermarking name. However, the solution is to incorporate an invisible text-into-image steganography with a warning that the image to be shared contains the name of the person who shares it. Another feasible solution will be incorporating an image-into-image steganography algorithm [a] within the messaging apps, where only the trusted person can decode the real image with a dedicated revealing method in [a] on the app side.
[a] Hiding images within images, TPAMI’19

Furthermore, such problem setting has a strong assumption that all the messaging apps have the proposed DeepRAFT system. Because if not, it is easy for the user to save the image and share it elsewhere. However, it is not possible to achieve such goal of requesting all companies to use DeepRAFT. By contrast, the aforementioned two possible solutions of watermarking names and image-into-image steganography have no such constraints, since the image either is modified with names or is not the real one without the dedicated image revealing tool, thus preventing the image from sharing elsewhere.

In the related work section, I saw that the authors claimed that image-into-image steganography method image does not consider rotation and cropping. But it is still unclear why not just improving prior work on this point, but develop such a sophisticated system. Also, the authors claim that “It is more noteworthy that none of previous studies considers the case of adversarial attacks by malicious actors”, which is overclaimed. In recent years of image steganography, most papers published on top conferences have explicitly considered the adversarial attack to the studied method. Only few works that are published before 2020 are limited in this aspect. In fact, the seminal work of Baluja has the discussions on adversarial attacks and proposes several possible solutions to defend their stagenography method, especially in their journal version [a].

- *Experiments:*

More ablation studies should be provided on the method side, to validate for example the choice of loss functions.

- *Minor:*

The punctuation for Eq. 2 is missing.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The paper is generally well-written.
- The studied problem of anti-forwarding seems novel and has potential usage in the industrial applications.
- I cannot judge the reproducibility of the devised system, given that the code is not provided
content.summary_of_the_review: My major concern is the problem setting of this work. It seems to me that there are already many possible solutions that are more computationally efficient, instead of devising a new complicated system.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
